  "overall_assessment": "Changes required: the core architecture follows the approved target, but the new CI parity guard leaves one explicit fail-closed protection obligation unenforced. SEC13-01 is a protection-harness defect established by source inspection, not a demonstrated tenant breakout or an observed false-green execution. Review scope is the embedded package only; no tools, edits, independent execution, or external retrieval were performed.\n\nSecurity framing: complexity big; security risk high; attack simulation required. Relevant surfaces are BFF session/CSRF and BU grants, public API-key/account scope, verified bot ingress, credential decryption and operation binding, provider acknowledgements, MessageAcceptance persistence, browser completion handling, Docker namespace admission, private-file masks, and CI checkout/lifecycle execution. The supplied local adversarial probes provide substantive simulation evidence for these boundaries. This review does not certify production, hosted CI, or activated human runtime behavior.\n\nArchitecture and decisions: D01/D08 are adherent: the narrow domain Channel accepts an opaque recipient, factories register implementations explicitly, and the independent fake exercises substitution through the real resolver/BFF/PostgreSQL path. The preserved physical origin enum and public numeric-phone contract are approved compatibility constraints. D02/D03 are adherent in the inspected paths: authorization precedes trusted references, credentials remain inside operation-specific adapters, and dispatch checks capture BU, identity, generation, epoch and official credential version. D04/D05 preserve conservative acknowledgement classification, one external invocation, bounded timeout, truthful uncertainty, and captured-key local readback. D06 retains the sole keyed MessageAcceptance owner and conditional current-owner finalization. D07 preserves deterministic origin selection, bot ingress pinning, whole-history window semantics and metadata-only availability. D09 provides one shared composition module and removes common sender dispatch branches; protocol-specific registration clients remain legitimate. D10 is partly adherent: browser protection and actual automated validation are supported, while the new guard's error-propagation protection is incomplete as detailed in SEC13-01. No temporary architectural exception or new provider/template/intent capability is justified or needed.\n\nTenant/auth/credential and dispatch fences: supplied negative mutations cover absent session, missing CSRF header, authenticated foreign BU access and foreign-account API-key sends with no provider output or disallowed OUT writes. Concurrent distinct tenants use different sealed tokens and provider resources with tenant-local Message readbacks. The pre-dispatch tests delegate to the shipping Meta/Evolution factories; their omission controls fail the intended 409-versus-201 assertion and record exact restoration. Real same-resource REAUTORIZAR and credential-version-only rotation are separately exercised. These support the approved distinction between generation changes and permissible post-dispatch credential resealing. Resolver availability remains observational and does not grant send authority. The acknowledged local-check-to-network interval remains a residual limitation rather than new drift.\n\nHistorical closure: preserve ST06-R01/R03/R04/R05 dispositions. Current Meta source rejects the recorded non-first/malformed acknowledgement and false/malformed success cases; Evolution distinguishes arbitrary 2xx {} from the approved key:{} acknowledgement. No fresh counterevidence establishes regression at those loci. Preserve PERF-02's recorded disposition and inline precision correction; do not create another follow-up obligation for it. SEC13-01 challenges the newly delivered CI protection mechanism with fresh source counterevidence.\n\nR02 causal barrier: the corrected instrumentation is installed before the held POST, forwards the native fetch response and body, observes native response.text() settlement, and waits for a subsequent browser task. In the embedded api.ts-to-Inbox success path, the generation/draft decision executes through promise continuations without another intervening await, so the task establishes the required ordering. Counts 1/1/1 prevent a vacuous completion assertion. Actual omission run30246 records the intended same-text draft failure with 49 other browser cases passing, unchanged test hash, a distinct served mutant bundle, and exact Inbox restoration. Current all2564 retains those restored source/test hashes and reports 50 browser passes. This supports closure of the previous protection gap; headers, network completion and animation frames are no longer the sole ordering evidence.\n\nPrivate-file, mask and CI trust boundaries: positive application bind inventories and freshness pathspecs avoid the prohibited broad application-root discovery. Application workspace overlays and explicit dotenv masks support the declared boundary; checks compare fictitious public masks before npm/product execution. The WSL translation is restricted to the declared socket/path form, and its temporary overlay retains the same three public mask sources. These observations do not prove excluded private paths clean or establish general host isolation. Namespace inventories now check each command's status before admission and cleanup eligibility; supplied actual-wrapper controls cover each listing failure, empty config-only success and collision refusal. Cleanup source preserves failure status, handles INT/TERM and reports failed down operations. The PR job uses the approved private checkout pattern and read-only repository permissions, with no publish/deploy step. Repository-authored runner and guard changes remain trusted CI code; the guard has a concrete error-masking blind spot.\n\nSchema/index/timeout and performance: the sole schema delta matches the approved managed composite Message index; its migration uses BEGIN/COMMIT and transaction-local 5s lock/60s statement bounds. Disposable deployment and SQLSTATE55P03/57014 rollback probes support the migration path. Accelerated 100ms/1ms abort probes do not prove actual 5s/60s elapsed durations, and are correctly disclosed. Preserved rows and absent aborted indexes are meaningful rollback assertions. The actual 500-reference plan constrains both conversation and direction IN, performs 500 index probes, removes zero rows by direction filtering, and reports 1003 shared hits/zero shared reads at 2.206ms. Only representative histories contain the heavy OUT suffix; many references are empty. This supports the access-path correction without establishing cold-cache or production capacity. Expired IN timestamps and equal-time ID selection remain observable. Selected non-window references issue zero latest-IN queries. The descriptive write sample reports 6,856,704 index bytes and 17.62ms versus 6.33ms for indexed/unindexed insertion batches; it demonstrates maintenance cost without a reliable universal ratio or SLO. Full-build write blocking and pending preserved-database migration remain operational constraints.\n\nValidation and claim limits: the current canonical command is CHANNELS_DOCKER_TRANSPORT=linux bash scripts/test-channels-local.sh all, with the recorded verified shared-socket context. all2564 reports exit0 and 194 API unit, 312 PostgreSQL E2E, 29 Web unit and 50 Chromium passes, with frozen-source and served/dist/preserved-bundle provenance. These are supplied execution records, not executions or hashes independently recomputed here. Earlier Linux failures are correctly classified as infrastructure failures. Windows API diagnostics passed; a current final Windows broad run is not supplied. Native Linux path controls do not establish hosted Ubuntu execution. Remote CI remains not_run and is not an additional prerequisite to the approved local milestone. Human database migration, API/Web activation, HTTPS restoration and fresh real IN/OUT on both bindings remain pending delivery gates. PCV candidates contain EPS strong-query evidence, FRC 20x5 retriggers, BCI 20x5 distinct-conversation overlap with per-owned readbacks, and a bounded RLS stage; independent reviewer binding and authoritative lane disposition remain pending. Distinct-conversation overlap does not establish same-key external exactly-once.\n\nTest-quality observations relevant to security: provider-interface test changes follow the real port change, and assertions include credentials/resources, persistence provenance, denied effects and retained drafts. The dependency guard, R05 regression, R02 omission and index-less PERF-01 runs provide specific fail-first or mutation evidence; they do not convert all historical test-after changes into test-first work. Provider doubles deliberately replace external boundaries while Nest wiring, auth, PostgreSQL and browser consumption remain real. No silent real-to-mock fallback is evident in these changed paths. The new guard's synthetic coverage misses shell-level swallowed failures, which materially limits its effectiveness despite the green current candidate. Separate complete TQA, Performance, Cutover and final gates remain required.\n\nThreat intelligence: no independent refresh was performed under the package-only/no-tools constraint. Embedded official Docker references provide provenance for the path-translation rationale; no current advisory/CVE clearance or newly retrieved security guidance is claimed. SEC13-01 derives entirely from embedded source.\n\nResidual risks and confidence: external dispatch cannot be atomically fenced with the local database; crash recovery and null-ID echo deduplication remain explicitly limited and handed to ST-CON-04. Live-provider operation, remote CI execution and preserved-database migration are unverified here. Confidence is moderate in the bounded automated candidate and strong in the source-level guard counterexample. Promotion candidate: require an error-masking mutation and observable nonzero-exit/cleanup proof whenever a project guard claims fail-closed shared-suite admission.",
  "recommended_path": "Remediate SEC13-01 within the existing approved guard/runner paths, add the missing negative control before the fix, freeze the revised bytes, and repeat canonical all plus focused independent review. Preserve prior resolved findings and the approved architecture. Keep migration, activation, operator IN/OUT, PCV disposition, consolidation and final gates pending; no waiver or production approval is implied.",

      "title": "The parity guard admits shell-level masking of required suite failures",
      "rationale": "scripts/check-channels-ci-parity.py:146 validates the shared lifecycle through ordered substring presence. Replacing the required command with `npm run test:e2e || true` preserves every required substring and its order. The existing missing-suite mutations still reject successfully, and fake_wrapper_checks runs config-only, exiting before RUNNER_SCRIPT execution. Consequently this mutation satisfies the guard while allowing an E2E failure to be ignored and a later successful browser command to determine an exit0 result. Appending `|| true` to the common guard invocation has the same presence-check weakness. This is source-demonstrable but was not executed in this review. The current supplied runner does propagate failures; the defect is that the newly required protection harness cannot detect this approval-breaking drift. D10 and the approved v1.3 proposal explicitly require rejection of bypasses and swallowed errors, so current green all2564 does not discharge this protection obligation. The blast radius is false acceptance of future shared local/CI validation, not a demonstrated application authorization exploit.",
      "suggested_action": "Option A (recommended): strengthen validation of the mandatory command invocations and failure propagation within the already admitted guard/runner paths. Add an actual mutation containing `npm run test:e2e || true` and require rejection; cover masking of the common guard invocation as well. Add a safe executable failure control proving that a failed required leaf produces nonzero wrapper exit and observable cleanup. Option B: use another bounded lifecycle-validation approach with equivalent executable negatives if it is simpler to maintain. Option C: retain the current checks; this leaves the explicit fail-closed harness obligation unsatisfied. Preserve the sole shared RUNNER_SCRIPT owner, restore/freeze the source, and collect fresh canonical all evidence after remediation.",
      "affected_paths": [
        "scripts/check-channels-ci-parity.py",
        "scripts/test-channels-local.sh"
      ]
    }
